hyps.why: With edge 0 severed node 1 is zero, so a conv on 1->3 has nothing to process and the edit is a no-op.
A conv on 0->3 shows diminishing returns when the output already receives a strong 3x3 conv via edge 5.
A conv on 1->3 adds less when a direct 3x3 conv on 0->3 already supplies the output with features.
Adding a shortcut where no direct path existed gains more than replacing an existing op, which is often a loss.
Replacing none with a conv adds capacity and a direct path, a bigger gain than swapping skip or pooling for conv.
Adding a conv to an absent edge brings new capacity and connectivity, more than replacing skip_connect.
Severing edge 0 is more damaging when edge 1 is also none, since the input then reaches the output mainly via edge 3.
Removing edge 5 costs more when it replaces a 3x3 conv than when it replaces skip or pooling.
Removing edge 2 costs almost nothing when edge 0 is none, because node 1 carries no signal to forward.
Dropping edge 4 hurts less when a direct 3x3 conv on 0->3 already feeds the output.
